description: The API architecture of Notation Systems: four roles a module's API may play, four planes the estate exposes, and the thirteen module families that map one onto the other. Closed, and derived rather than declared per capability — a capability names the family it belongs to, and the role and plane follow from this table. A per-capability role written by hand would drift the way a written-down count does; a family that changes its treatment changes it once, here, for every capability in it.

invariant.statement: Every API response either carries a canonical reference and a proof root, or says explicitly that it is an operational observation and states its limitations.
invariant.why: A response with neither is the dangerous shape: it reads as authoritative, cannot be verified, and nothing in it says which. The two kinds are not a spectrum. A snapshot fold of a signed journal is a claim about canonical state and must be checkable against the chain that carries it; a liveness probe is one process's opinion of itself at a moment, and saying so is what stops it being read as the estate's state.

referenced.description: Carries a canonical `notation://` reference and the proof root the value was read at

operational_observation.description: An observation of a running system, true of that process at that moment and of nothing else

public_read.description: Publicly readable. The response is a read of held material, bounded by tenant and by what the reader is authorized to see.

proof_verifiable.description: Proof-verifiable. The caller supplies or names something and gets back a verification result that can be re-derived independently; the module never mutates what it verifies.

governed_write.description: Internally writable, and only through a governed pipeline. There is no direct canonical CRUD: a write is a submission that a named gate admits or refuses.

host_infrastructure.description: Host-only. Exposes capability and status, never storage, credentials, provider control or raw internals.

plane.description: Served on the planes its family admits. Every plane rule applies.

operator_local.description: Not served on any plane. An action a human operator triggers — a key rotation, a credential issue, a site activation, a runtime switch — rather than an endpoint anyone calls.
operator_local.why: Every estate has actions that are not API, and they are usually the dangerous ones: they mint credentials, rotate keys, activate releases and switch providers. Forcing them onto a plane so the model looks tidy is how such an action acquires a route. Naming the exposure instead makes the set countable, and makes 'can a model trigger anything that mints a credential or activates a release?' a question with an answer — which is why the forbidden surfaces are the machine-reachable ones. A person decides; an agent does not get to.

tenant_read.title: Tenant Read API
tenant_read.description: Corpus, projection, search, releases, timelines, proof navigation. Every read is bound to a tenant and returns references, not unrestricted data.

verification.title: Verification API
verification.description: Any supported VerificationEnvelope, closure, checks, Warrant Graph. Answers whether something verifies, and against what root.

governance.title: Governance API
governance.description: Coverage, source-policy windows, retention, readiness, preflight, replay, challenges. Typed evidence and explicit non-authorization: a readiness answer is never an approval.

internal_operator.title: Internal Ingestion / Operator API
internal_operator.description: Signed federation packets and controlled operational actions. Never public canonical CRUD, and never a route by which a reader becomes a writer.

kernel.treatment: Universal reference resolution and proof verification; never direct mutation
never: direct mutation of anything it resolves or verifies

persistence.treatment: Internal persistence adapters; public API reads only through tenant-bound resolvers
never: a public route into the store
a read that is not tenant-bound
persistence.note: `host_infrastructure` describes what the module's API affords, not what the module does. A persistence adapter obviously writes; what it must never offer is a route by which a caller writes through it. A write that lands durably reaches the store through governed ingestion, so it is declared `acquisition` and the store stays behind it.

acquisition.treatment: Read policy/receipt/retention status; writes only through governed ingestion
never: an ingestion that bypasses the policy window

corpus.treatment: Corpus catalog, build comparison, membership, provenance, and time-bound read APIs
never: an admission that is not an explicit validation step
corpus.note: The table lists `admission` here, and its treatment sentence is read-shaped: catalog, comparison, membership, provenance, time-bound reads. Admission is the write — the explicit validation step COR-006 requires — so it sits in `acquisition`, whose treatment is exactly 'writes only through governed ingestion'. The check found this: four admission capabilities declared `corpus` and were refused for executing in a role that does not mutate.

projection.treatment: Projection catalog plus bounded query endpoints with exact proof roots
never: a write back to what it projects

agent.treatment: Tenant-bound agent/API tools; return references and authorization state, not unrestricted data
never: returning material the caller is not authorized to hold

release.treatment: Release and trust-status endpoints; activation and signing stay operator-only
never: activation or signing on a public plane
release.note: The table pairs read and write here as `corpus` did: 'Release and trust-status endpoints' are the API, while 'activation and signing stay operator-only'. Those two are not endpoints at all, and they carry `api_exposure: operator_local` — off every plane, triggered by a person.

readiness.treatment: Governance/readiness APIs with typed evidence, exceptions, and explicit non-authorization
never: a readiness answer that reads as an authorization

operations.treatment: Operations APIs for lag, replay state, bounded health, and evidence — not provider control
operations.note: 'not provider control' is the operative half. Lag, replay state, bounded health and evidence are operations APIs; starting a loop or switching a model is provider control, and is `infrastructure` with `operator_local` exposure. The check found two of those on an HTTP surface with no plane that admits them.

topology.treatment: Architecture/topology APIs with logical views and no raw security details

federation.treatment: Internal signed-packet ingestion plus acknowledgements, replay reports, and audit reads

adjudication.treatment: Governance/research APIs for candidates, reviews, reproducibility, and outcomes
never: a computation result presented as a measurement

infrastructure.treatment: Infrastructure modules; expose capability/status only, not storage or credential controls

deviation.description: A sentence recording that a capability does not fit the architecture, and why it is still served. Required when a capability's declared family cannot admit what it does — most often a write reachable on a machine surface that no plane should carry.
deviation.why: The estate deploys systems it did not write. Forcing every one of their surfaces into a family that fits would make the architecture describe a system nobody runs; refusing to place them would leave the write paths uncounted. A declared deviation does neither: it is a write the architecture would not serve, named, countable, and attached to the thing that has it. The catalog already records corpus failures this way, for the same reason — a record that cannot express a failure records only flattery.
